identity_evidence.quote: A 61-year-old Thailand male with end-stage kidney disease due to diabetic nephropathy underwent a living-unrelated donor kidney transplantation

attribution_limitations: The sentences about no perioperative complications and about discharge with a serum creatinine value sit in the past-illness paragraph after the transplant induction regimen, but do not name which operation or admission they refer to.

The biopsy result states a suspicion of chronic active ABMR followed by borderline acute T-cell-mediated rejection and secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in one list; it is unclear whether suspicion covers all three entries.

The Imaging examinations section says no imaging examinations were performed, while the history documents abdominal ultrasonography and liver MRI before surgery. The heading "CASE PRESENTATION / Imaging examinations" does not state the time scope.
A later tacrolimus trough target is printed as ng/dL while every other tacrolimus concentration in the case is in ng/mL.

The outcome paragraph says creatinine returned to baseline by postoperative day 7 coinciding with normalization of tacrolimus C0 and liver function tests, while the laboratory paragraph says transaminases returned to normal by postoperative day 10; the figure plots later values for transaminases and bilirubin on day 7. The word baseline is not tied to a specific value.

The abstract and discussion attribute the tacrolimus rise to reduced liver mass and function and ischemic injury, and the discussion says the estimated resection was accompanied by prolonged cold ischemia time and reperfusion injury; these are the authors' interpretation, and the case text does not describe how cold ischemia applied to a wedge resection.
The discussion says the authors hypothesized toxicity was driven by abnormally high peak concentrations reflected by C0; this is a hypothesis.
Several creatinine values are given as the starting point of a stated rise without their own time.
